chapter_theme: Sayujyam, union with Siva, the last of the four states: Saivam is relation with Siva, knowing oneself and reaching him, and its end is Siva's bliss; sayujyam is the state beyond waking, abiding in stillness and becoming Siva.
structure_note: Two verses built on anaphora: four lines on சைவம் (1512), four on சாயுச்சியம் (1513).

1512.reading: Saivam is relation with Siva; Saivam is knowing oneself and reaching Siva; Saivam is leaving what does not reach Siva; Saivam is Siva's bliss, sayujyam.
1512.nuance: சைவந் தனையறிந்து may be 'knowing Saivam' or 'knowing oneself (தன்னை)'. Line 3, சிவந்தன்னைச் சாராமல் நீங்குதல், can mean leaving all that is not Siva, or (less likely) parting without clinging even to Siva. The verse defines Saivam not as a sect but as a relation that ends in union.

1513.reading: Sayujyam is reaching the state beyond waking; sayujyam is abiding in stillness; sayujyam is becoming Siva; endless sayujyam is the power of bliss in the mind.
1513.nuance: சாக்கிராதீதம் (beyond waking) and உபசாந்தம் (complete stilling) are technical terms for the soul's highest states in Siddhanta. மனத்து ஆனந்த சத்தி may be 'the bliss-shakti in the mind' or a name of the Goddess as bliss.
